title: Nine arrested with 5,213 board feet of tanguile in Santa Marcela
summary: Acting on a resident's tip, police from the 1st Apayao Provincial Mobile Force Company and the Santa Marcela Municipal Police Station, with DENR-CENRO personnel, caught nine men loading tanguile flitches into a dump truck in Barangay Sipa on 2 February 2026. The lumber totalled 5,213.3 board feet with an estimated market value of P365,071. The suspects, seven from Pudtol, one from Kabugao and one from La Trinidad, Benguet, could not present transport permits and are held at the Santa Marcela police station for violation of Presidential Decree 705.
referredTo: DENR-CENRO (Apayao) and Santa Marcela Municipal Police Station

timeline.note: A resident tipped police about undocumented forest products being transported in Barangay Sipa.
Nine men were arrested while loading 5,213.3 board feet of tanguile flitches into a dump truck; charges under PD 705 were prepared.

title: P133M quarry equipment seized inside Angono subdivision project
summary: On 20 January 2026 the DENR raided unauthorised mineral extraction inside the Village East II Residential Subdivision Project in Angono after surveillance showed mobile crushers running and aggregates being hauled to a dump site near the materials recovery facility along the Taytay-Angono Road in Barangay Kalayaan. Heavy machinery, trucks, mobile crushers and stockpiled aggregates worth about P133 million were seized. The Environmental Management Bureau Region IV-A issued a cease and desist order the same day, and an inquest case for theft of minerals under Section 103 of the Philippine Mining Act was filed before the Rizal Provincial Prosecutor. The Angono local government, which had ordered the site closed in 2014, backed the DENR action.
referredTo: DENR-EMB Region IV-A and Provincial Prosecutor of Rizal

timeline.note: Enforcement teams seized about P133 million in equipment and aggregates and served a cease and desist order on the subdivision project.
An inquest complaint for theft of minerals under RA 7942 was filed before the Provincial Prosecutor of Rizal against company officers and equipment operators.
Mayor Gerardo Calderon's administration said it remained opposed to quarrying at the site and backed the DENR case.

title: Cease and desist order stops Fortuna Mining exploration in Subic
summary: On 4 May 2026 the DENR Mines and Geosciences Bureau Regional Office 3, under Regional Director Noel B. Lacadin, ordered Fortuna Mining Corporation to cease and desist from exploration in Barangay Cawag, Subic. The company was exploring under Exploration Permit No. EP-001-2026-III without proof of consultation and endorsement by the local Sanggunian and without a National Commission on Indigenous Peoples certification, both required before implementing its work program. The permit also covers Pundakit in San Antonio and Looc and Balaybay in Castillejos. Subic officials said the company agreed to remove all equipment from the site.

timeline.note: Notice of Fortuna Mining's exploration permit application (EXPA000278 III) was posted.

title: Unauthorised Laguna de Bay reclamation in Taguig ordered stopped
summary: On 17 August 2026 the Philippine Reclamation Authority wrote to Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon ordering a stop to unauthorised reclamation along Laguna de Bay in Taguig, and on 20 August the DPWH issued cease and desist orders covering flood control, slope protection and multi-purpose projects along the Taguig lakeshore, acting on directives from the Office of the President. Dizon said the earth-filling had disrupted natural drainage channels and worsened monsoon flooding, and that unpermitted reclaimed areas are subject to forfeiture to the national government. Senator Panfilo Lacson said at least P3.713 billion in public funds had gone into projects on the reclaimed areas and identified four parcels with fraudulently issued titles. Dizon said no government-funded structures would be demolished.
referredTo: Philippine Reclamation Authority and DPWH Metro Manila 1st District Engineering Office

timeline.note: The PRA ordered the DPWH to halt all unauthorised reclamation and infrastructure works in the Laguna de Bay area of Taguig.
Cease and desist orders were issued against projects tied to the alleged illegal reclamation, on directive from the Office of the President.
The DPWH publicly announced the orders and convened Taguig City, the LLDA and the Pasig River Urban Development Project.
Lacson said at least P3.713 billion in public funds were spent on projects in the reclaimed areas and flagged four parcels with fraudulent titles.

title: Resort inside Sierra Madre protected area shut down in Infanta
summary: DENR Region IV-A personnel from CENRO Real, with the Infanta Municipal Police Station, the Quezon Police Mobile Force Company, the Army's 80th Infantry Battalion and the Infanta local government, served and enforced a cease and desist order on a resort, identified by residents as Lola's Haven Resort, built inside the national park, wildlife sanctuary and game preserve declared under Presidential Proclamation No. 1636 of 1977. The operator was cited for unauthorised construction of facilities and running tourism activities without Protected Area Management Board clearance or DENR permits, in violation of RA 7586 as amended by RA 11038, and was fined P50,000.

timeline.actor: DENR-CENRO Real with PNP, Army and Infanta LGU
timeline.note: A cease and desist order was served on the resort for illegal structures and tourism activities inside the PP 1636 protected area, with a P50,000 fine.

title: Coast Guard intercepts 2,000 board feet of lawaan at Rio Hondo
summary: Acting on intelligence that a motorised banca carrying undocumented timber had left Latuan, Basilan, Philippine Coast Guard personnel intercepted the vessel at about 8:30 p.m. on 4 August 2026 in Barangay Rio Hondo, Zamboanga City. About 2,000 board feet of lawaan lumber without DENR transport permits were seized and brought to Coast Guard Station Zamboanga, and the boat operator was taken in for profiling. The banca was left at its docking area because of hull damage.

timeline.note: A banca from Latuan, Basilan carrying about 2,000 board feet of undocumented lawaan was intercepted at Rio Hondo.
The lumber was held at the station and the operator profiled for violating forestry transport rules.

title: Illegal gold mining raids in Barobo net arrests and heavy equipment
summary: On 27 June 2026 police with the DENR Mines and Geosciences Bureau and the Monitoring and Information Assistance Center raided an illegal mining site in Barangay Bahi, Barobo, arresting three men aged 33, 34 and 45 from Tagbina who could not show mining permits. Police estimated the seized water pumps and backhoe at P5 million; a later report listed a Volvo backhoe, pumps, chainsaws, hoses and tools worth P7.1 million. The suspects face charges under the Philippine Mining Act of 1995. Barobo Mayor Ronnie Martizano said he was disgusted that the raid was mounted without coordinating with the municipality, which had allowed limited gold panning pending Minahang Bayan approval. Earlier, on 4 February, DENR Region XIII's enforcement division and 24 PNP Special Action Force personnel busted another site in Barangay Guinhalinan, arresting five people including two foreigners.

timeline.actor: DENR Region XIII Enforcement Division and PNP-SAF

title: MGB suspends Woggle exploration permit in Dupax del Norte
summary: Mines and Geosciences Bureau Director Michael Cabalda suspended the exploration permit of Woggle Corporation, a British-owned affiliate of FCF Minerals, in Dupax del Norte as a preventive measure to defuse tension after months of community opposition, barricades at Sitio Upper Tacbao in Barangay Bitnong, the burning of a Woggle wheel excavator in December 2025 and the arrest of at least seven protesters on court orders. Woggle said it received the order on 11 February 2026, questioned its legal and contractual basis, and noted that over 1,200 employees and contractors of its Runruno operations depend on continued exploration. Cabalda said lifting the suspension depends on the situation improving.
referredTo: Mines and Geosciences Bureau central office

timeline.note: A Woggle heavy wheel excavator trapped behind a barricade in Barangay Bitnong was burned, according to the BusinessMirror account.
The exploration permit was suspended as a preventive measure to prevent any untoward incident; Woggle formally received the order the same day.
The company disputed the legal basis of the suspension and asked the MGB for clear justification, citing 1,200 dependent workers.

title: Undocumented lumber sold on Facebook seized in Tamugan, Davao City
summary: On 16 July 2026 DENR XI's CENRO Davao, with the PNP Maritime Group, raided a lumber outlet in Lower Tamugan, Barangay Tamugan, Marilog District that was selling forest products through Facebook Marketplace. Its lumber dealer registration had expired in 2024 and was never renewed despite notices. Officers confiscated 240 pieces of lumber and flitches totalling 2,198.66 board feet (72 falcata, 38 mahogany, 82 narra and 48 miscellaneous) appraised at P82,133.89, plus a bandsaw unit worth P50,000. Charges were prepared under PD 705, RA 460 and DENR Administrative Orders 2021-05 and 97-32.

timeline.actor: DENR XI CENRO Davao and PNP Maritime Group
timeline.note: 240 pieces of undocumented lumber and a bandsaw were seized from an outlet whose dealer permit had lapsed in 2024.

title: Arbor Day volunteers plant 7,460 seedlings across Central Visayas
summary: For Philippine Arbor Day on 25 June 2026, DENR 7 under Director Laudemir Salac mobilised 1,139 volunteers who planted 7,460 native and fruit-bearing seedlings on 5.72 hectares at six sites: Barangay Lusaran in Cebu City (1,500 seedlings), Santo Niño in Malabuyoc (2,000), Kangaibe on Bantayan Island (1,000), Nug-as in Alcoy (1,000), Punta Cruz in Maribojoc, Bohol (1,600) and Puerto San Pedro in Bien Unido, Bohol (360). Species included cinnamon, narra, molave, lauan, agoho and bungalon. The Cebu provincial government separately planted 4,200 fruit-bearing and mangrove seedlings in Tuburan, Talisay City, Naga City, Dalaguete and San Fernando from 24 to 27 June with about 280 volunteers. Nationally, the DENR reported 1,673,572 seedlings planted on 2,347.23 hectares that day and shifted to post-planting watering, maintenance and survival monitoring.

timeline.note: A province-led drive began in Tuburan and ran through 27 June, planting 4,200 seedlings across five LGUs.

The DENR adopted a post-planting monitoring framework focused on watering, maintenance and protection of planting sites.

title: San Fernando council recalls Altai mining endorsement on Sibuyan
summary: On 17 July 2026 the Sangguniang Bayan of San Fernando passed Municipal Resolution No. 297 endorsing Altai Philippines Mining Corporation's proposed operations under its Mineral Production Sharing Agreement in Barangay España, Sibuyan Island, near Mt. Guiting-Guiting Natural Park. After protests, the council voted 4-2 on 3 August to withdraw the endorsement, citing procedural infirmities and deteriorating peace and order, and required broader consultations, environmental studies and natural capital accounting under RA 11995 before any reconsideration. Altai said it would pursue all legal and administrative remedies. MGB MIMAROPA Regional Director Felizardo Gacad Jr. said a cease and desist order issued in 2023 remains in effect, the company's exploration period expired in 2024 with an extension refused, and no mining activity has been detected.

timeline.note: The council approved Resolution No. 297 endorsing Altai's mining project in Barangay España.
In a special session the council voted 4-2 to recall the endorsement and ordered further studies and public consultations.
The company said the quick withdrawal raised questions and that it would use every legal and administrative remedy available.
Director Gacad said the 2023 cease and desist order stands and agency monitoring has found no mining or exploration activity on the site.
